source_block.bori: BORI CE Shalya Parva, Debroy translation vol. 7 (chapter-level citations): opening chapters — Kripa's counsel of peace, Duryodhana's refusal, Ashvatthama proposes Shalya, Shalya consecrated, Vasudeva's counsel to Yudhishthira; the eighteenth-day array; the Bhima–Shalya mace fight; Yudhishthira's advance; Shalya unhorsed with sword and shield; the gold-and-gem dart and Shalya's fall 'as if embracing the earth'; Sahadeva slays Shakuni; Duryodhana flees alone into the lake (Dvaipayana).

source_block.divergence: Section/adhyaya numbers follow the vulgate (Ganguli = Gita Press); BORI CE chapters are cited at chapter-group level only. Kinship: Shalya is the brother of Madri, uncle of Nakula and Sahadeva and so kin to all the Pandavas; Ganguli has Krishna call him the maternal uncle — we narrate only 'your kin'. Omitted for length: the deaths of Shalya's younger brother and the Madra guard, Kritavarma's rescue after the mace fight, Shalya's fierce duels with the twins, Satyaki and Dhrishtadyumna, Bhima's part in unhorsing Shalya, Duryodhana's illusion that stills the lake. Shalya's fall is narrated and shown only through his fallen crown — no body.
